ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3 (2024), Beneficial Owner Information Administration Measures (effective 1 November 2024); Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615); Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) significant controllers register provisions; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong holding/investment entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the High Court of Hong Kong if the origin and destination are both Apostille Convention states; Consular Legalization through the PRC Embassy/Consulate if the destination is a non-member state. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry or equivalent competent registry in the document origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille under the Hague Apostille Convention if the issuing state is a Convention member; Consular Legalization through notarization, competent ministry authentication, and the PRC consular post if the issuing state is not a Convention member. Apostille and Consular Legalization are alternative single paths, not cumulative steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the Foreign-Invested Partnership formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the investing company and notary public in the issuing jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Single-step Hague Apostille for Convention states; single-channel Consular Legalization for non-member states. Because these are mutually exclusive, an apostilled document must not be subsequently consular-legalized.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Foreign-Invested Partnership Agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary or legal counsel, certified by the relevant registry or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuer is in an Apostille Convention state; Consular Legalization if the issuer is in a non-member state. Both routes are independent alternatives; parallel processing must not include sequential chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each non-resident partner and authorized representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank maintaining the partner account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For banks in Apostille Convention states: notarized signature plus apostille only. For banks in non-member states: notarization plus consular legalization at the destination consulate. The two authentication protocols are mutually exclusive and must not be combined or sequenced.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before formation, every general partner, limited partner, beneficial owner, authorized signatory, franchise master licensee, royalty payee, and bank account mandate must be screened against OFAC SDN/SSI lists, UN Security Council Resolution 1267/1988 and successor sanctions, EU restrictive measures, Hong Kong United Nations Sanctions Ordinance Cap. 610 lists, PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions announcements, and PBOC/AMLO adverse-media and domestic watch lists. PEPs, immediate family, and close associates require senior management approval, enhanced due diligence, verified source of wealth, and periodic review. The OFAC 50% rule applies to any entity owned fifty percent or more by a sanctioned person; lower-level ownership still requires risk-based evaluation and continuous transaction monitoring for at least five years after relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Search and online name reservation/incorporation service (esearch.cr.gov.hk); for the PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership leg, the local Market Regulation Administration one-window enterprise registration and name clearance portal operating on the SAMR National Enterprise Registration Information System.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: For the PRC FIP, the statutory Chinese name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division + selected trade name + industry or operational characteristic + organization form, using standard simplified Chinese characters only; an English or Pinyin transliterated supplementary name may be used for branding but cannot replace the Chinese statutory name. In Hong Kong, an English name and an optional Chinese name may be reserved; the Chinese name, if adopted, must be a phonetic transliteration or semantic equivalent acceptable to the Companies Registry and must not contain prohibited official or sensitive tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is refused, the applicant must obtain the written rejection notice stating the statutory ground. Within 30 days from rejection, a formal reconsideration or administrative appeal must be filed with the next-higher Administration for Market Regulation, attaching the original application, the rejection notice, corrected alternative names, third-party consent letters for any named enterprises, and evidence that the proposed token is not misleading. If the reviewer affirms the rejection, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration within 60 days or institute administrative litigation under the PRC Administrative Litigation Law within six months. In Hong Kong, the applicant may request written review by the Companies Registry and, if still refused, seek judicial review before the Court of First Instance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the sole registered office for the Foreign-Invested Partnership in this industry. The Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department, the PRC State Taxation Administration, and AML-compliant banks will reject a mailbox-only address for a food-franchise and royalty business because physical business records, staff presence, and operating premises are required for business registration, municipal food business licensing, franchise filings, and corporate account onboarding. A virtual office may be used only as a supplementary correspondence address where the primary address remains a physical commercial premise leased in the name of the partnership and registered with the local Market Regulation Administration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist: (1) registered office signage; (2) physical self-serve food premises; (3) lease and utility evidence; (4) payroll and social-insurance records; (5) inventory, equipment, and food-safety records; (6) tax, VAT, and royalty-receipt ledgers. Unannounced inspection probability is quantified as high, 80 to 90 percent in the first 12 months for food premises by municipal Market Regulation Administration and food-health authorities; moderate, 40 to 60 percent, for registered-office and commercial-substance checks by tax authorities if a virtual address is used; and low, 10 to 20 percent, for bank site-visit due diligence once physical premises and financial records are corroborated.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of the Laws of Hong Kong, specifically sections 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10; Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38); Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), sections 2, 5 and 6; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) for banking compliance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnership Section, 15/F, Queensway Government Offices, Hong Kong SAR; and Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Limited Partnership (Form LP1) due with the Registrar of Companies, together with Statement of Business Particulars (Form IRBR 1) to the Business Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a Hong Kong limited partnership. The partners are free to fix capital contributions by deed. There is no blocked escrow account rule under the Limited Partnership Ordinance; however, in practice capital subscriptions may be held in an escrow account pending drawdown call notices.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (FIP) — PASSED AT THE INAUGURAL MEETING OF THE MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE, HELD AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE AT [ADDRESS], ON [DATE], IN THE PRESENCE OF THE GENERAL PARTNER AND BY UNANIMOUS CONSENT. WHEREAS this Partnership has been duly constituted as a limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of the Laws of Hong Kong and is to be registered under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310); WHEREAS the partners intend to establish the management, capital, banking and statutory compliance framework for the business of fast-casual self-serve broth bowl master licensing; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Limited Partnership Deed, together with the Schedule of Capital Contributions annexed thereto, is hereby ratified. Each partner shall pay his or her committed capital into the Partnership's dedicated escrow trust account within five business days of the issuance of a drawdown notice signed by the General Partner. The subscription price, ratios, profit-sharing percentages and allocation methodology, as set out in Clause 7 of the Deed, are adopted as binding. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Partnership shall open and maintain an operating account, a royalty settlement account and a payroll account at [Bank] and such other financial institutions as the General Partner may approve. All cheques, electronic transfers, and money market instruments shall be signed by the General Partner and the Compliance Officer jointly, and for amounts exceeding HKD 100,000, by at least three authorized persons designated in the Banking Mandate. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Partnership shall be physically located at [Registered Address in Hong Kong], and the same shall be the official address for service of legal process and all statutory notices. The General Partner is authorized to execute the registered office agreement and to file the office address with the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS: The following persons are appointed with effect from the formation date: (a) the General Partner, who shall have the power to manage the Partnership's business; (b) the Designated Partnership Representative, who shall be named as the business contact person on the Business Registration Certificate; (c) the Anti-Money Laundering and Compliance Officer, who shall supervise continuing obligations under Cap. 615; and (d) the Master License Registrar, who shall be responsible for issuance, renewal and enforcement of self-serve broth bowl master franchise licenses. 5. STATUTORY FILINGS: The Designated Partnership Representative is directed to file Form LP1, present the Business Registration Particulars, and make all necessary applications to the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Fire Services Department, and Labour Department. 6. DURATION: This resolution shall be effective from the date passed and shall remain in force until revoked in writing by the General Partner. — PASSED AND ADOPTED: [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Registration of the Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Limited Partnership Section (Online e-Registry portal and paper filing counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before filing, conduct a name-search on the Companies Registry's Integrated Information System to confirm the proposed name is not identical to an existing company or partnership. Prepare and execute the Limited Partnership Deed setting out capital, management, distributions and dissolution, and have each general and limited partner sign. Complete and submit Form LP1 (Application for Registration of Limited Partnership) together with the deed and the prescribed fee, either by post to 15/F, Queensway Government Offices, or electronically via the e-Registry portal, ensuring that all statutory particulars of partners are correct. Upon acceptance, the Registrar will issue a Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership. Adjust the deed and submit again if any notation or requisition is raised by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 (signed by general and limited partners)
Executed Limited Partnership Deed with Schedule of Capital Contributions
Certified true copy of each partner's identity document or corporate registration certificate
Consent to act as General Partner (signed)
Proposed registered office address in Hong Kong with proof of address (tenancy agreement or utility bill)
Payment of prescribed LP registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition, respond in writing within 14 calendar days with a conformed Form LP1 or additional supporting declarations. If the application is suspended or rejected, amend the deed to resolve any name conflict or statutory defect and re-file with a fresh fee, or apply for a name change by deed of alteration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the Registrar's Certificate of Registration, deliver Form IRBR 1 (Application for Business Registration) to the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department, enclosing a certified true copy of the Limited Partnership Registration Certificate, a copy of the partnership deed, and the full residential addresses of each partner. The form must be co-signed by the general partner and the tax-designated partnership representative. Upon approval, the Business Registration Office will issue a Business Registration Certificate and the business registration number (BRN). The certificate must be displayed prominently at all business premises, and annual renewal must be completed before the expiry date to avoid penalties under Cap. 310.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR 1
Certified true copy of Limited Partnership Registration Certificate
Certified copy of the Limited Partnership Deed
Identity documents and residential addresses of all partners
Lease or tenancy agreement for business premises
Business Registration fee and levy receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office queries the submission, provide additional evidence of the address or partner particulars within 21 working days. For late filing, obtain the prescribed penalty form and pay the fixed charge to regularize before the matter is referred to the Collector of Revenue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and AML Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed bank (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered, Bank of China (Hong Kong)) and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's AML/CTF supervisory framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business Registration Certificate, present the executed partnership deed, the LP registration certificate, business registration certificate, identity proofs of all beneficial owners, and a projected cash-flow statement to the licensed bank. The bank's compliance unit will conduct CDD and source-of-funds verification in line with the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615). The designated AML officer must sign the bank's corporate structure declaration. With the account, open segregated sub-accounts for royalty settlement and capital drawdowns, and establish dual-signature control as per the Banking Mandate. The bank may also request a copy of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department license if a physical restaurant outlet is operational.
required_dossiers: Executed Limited Partnership Deed
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Beneficial ownership declaration forms
Source of funds documentation (bank statements, audited accounts, tax receipts)
Passport or Hong Kong identity card of each partner and the designated AML officer
Board resolution naming signatories and limits (the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional CDD, respond within 10 business days with the requested corporate structure chart, certified ownership chain, and any regulatory licenses. If the application is declined, approach a second bank with an enhanced onboarding memorandum and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority referral letter, if previously issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business and Restaurant Licensing for Physical Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD), Licensing Section, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a completed Food Business Licence application (Form FEHB 197) to the Relevant Authority of the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, along with the tenancy agreement, the stamped deposit received, a scaled floor plan showing the self-serve broth bar layout, drainage and grease trap design, and a waste management plan. If the operation includes a central kitchen manufacturing broth concentrate, file a separate Food Factory Licence application. The premises will be inspected by environmental health officers and food inspectors prior to approval. The FEHD will issue a General Restaurant Licence upon compliance, subject to approved sanitation, ventilation, refuse storage and water supply standards. The licence must be renewed every three years.
required_dossiers: Form FEHB 197 (Food Business / Restaurant Licence application)
Tenancy agreement and proof of lawful occupancy
Scaled floor plan (1:100) of the self-serve broth station and kitchen
Grease trap, drainage, sewage, and waste disposal design
Ventilation and air conditioning system plan
Declaration of compliance with Food Safety Ordinance and food hygiene regulations
Bioproduct source declaration for broth ingredients and allergen management plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FEHD raises an objection, correct the floor plan or facilities within 30 days and re-submit for inspection. If the licence is refused, appeal to the Food Business Appeal Tribunal under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X) within one month. For small deficiencies, the FEHD may issue a notice of rectification allowing a re-inspection without a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Safety, Building Control and Occupational Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Fire Services Department (FSD), Buildings Department (BD), and Labour Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage an authorized fire service contractor to inspect the premises and install fire alarms, emergency lighting and extinguishers in accordance with the Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings. File Form LA1 with the Fire Services Department to obtain a Fire Service Installations and Equipment Compliance Certificate. In parallel, have the building owner inspect for structural integrity and obtain a Certificate of Compliance for the proposed use from the Buildings Department. Finally, secure an Occupational Safety Approval from the Labour Department under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance for the kitchen and service areas, including a hazard assessment of the self-serve broth stations, anti-scalding measures, and slip-resistant floor certification.
required_dossiers: Form LA1 to Fire Services Department
Architectural floor plan with fire escape routes
Fire service installation certificate from an approved contractor
Certificate of Compliance (Building) for the premises
Occupational safety and health risk assessment
Staff training certificates for fire safety and chemical handling
Emergency response plan and first aid signage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fire Services Department requires modifications, complete the remediation within 21 days and request an expedited re-inspection. For building control failures, engage an authorized person to submit revised plans to the Buildings Department for approval. For occupational safety, submit a revised hazard assessment and training records for further review; if the department imposes a penalty notice, make immediate rectification and apply for a reduction of fines through a mitigation hearing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) of the Hong Kong SAR, with mandatory coordination with the Fire Services Department, Buildings Department, Environmental Protection Department and Labour Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Restaurant Licence (Food Business Licence) under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X); if a central broth kitchen is established, a Food Factory Licence is additionally required; the master franchise trademark activity also requires Business Registration renewal under Cap. 310.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), The Government of the Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - not a designated project under Schedule 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499). The premises must only comply with the water pollution and waste disposal regulations as applicable to food service establishments, and no full EIA report is required unless the operation expands into a food processing facility beyond the threshold scale in paragraph 10(1) of Schedule 2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent must meet the standards in the Technical Memorandum on Effluent Discharge (Gazette as amended): BOD5 not exceeding 200 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 200 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 50 mg/L, pH within 6.0-10.0. Kitchen exhaust must not cause ambient VOCs above 15 mg/m3 at the site boundary; if frying or broth-cooking occurs, a mechanical ventilation and filtration system must be installed and registered with EPD under the Air Pollution Control Ordinance. Hazardous waste, such as waste cooking oil, must be removed by a licensed collector under the Waste Disposal Ordinance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Service Installations and Equipment Certificate under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap. 95), building occupancy certificate/structural compliance under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), and Occupational Safety and Health compliance under Cap. 509, including a hazard assessment of the self-serve broth stations with anti-scalding, slip-resistance, and emergency evacuation approvals.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, including its Business Registration Office (BRO), with the electronic tax filing portal 'eTAX' accessible via the HKSAR Government website. The BRO is located at Revenue Tower, 5 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), every person or entity carrying on business in Hong Kong, including a foreign-invested partnership (FIP), must apply for a Business Registration Certificate (BRC) within one month of commencing business. The procedure for a foreign non-resident partnership is: (1) Execute and provide the partnership agreement (or signed certified extract); (2) prepare and sign Form IRBR1 - Application for Business Registration (for sole proprietorships and partnerships); (3) attach certified true copies of identification documents for all partners (passport or national identity card, and for corporate partners, certificate of incorporation or equivalent and certificate of good standing); (4) provide proof of the Hong Kong principal place of business (e.g., tenancy agreement, rate demand, or utility bill) and the partners' residential/business addresses; (5) pay the prescribed Business Registration Fee and Protection of Wages on Insolvency Levy; (6) submit the application and documents to the Business Registration Office of the IRD, in person or by post. Upon approval, the IRD issues a BRC bearing a Business Registration Number which serves as the entity's tax payer identification number (TIN) for all Hong Kong tax filings and correspondence with the IRD. There is no separate VAT identification number because Hong Kong imposes no VAT/GST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Hong Kong does not operate any check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election mechanisms. A partnership is automatically fiscally transparent; each partner is severally assessed to profits tax on its own share of partnership profits. Individual partners may separately elect for Personal Assessment under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, but that is a personal election of the partner, not an entity-level election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax - Hong Kong levies no general consumption tax; the Dutiable Commodities Ordinance (Cap. 109) applies only to specified alcoholic drinks, tobacco, hydrocarbon oil, and methyl alcohol.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - there is no VAT/GST registration threshold. Every business operating in Hong Kong must hold a Business Registration Certificate as a condition of legal operation; turnover governs only the amount of the Business Registration fee and levy.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Hong Kong does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, electronic invoice APIs, or anti-fraud digital stamping. Commercial invoices may be issued in any format, but the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) requires that business records, including invoices and receipts, be retained for not less than seven years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Hong Kong has no VAT or GST and therefore no zero-rating of exports. Exports of goods or services from Hong Kong are outside the charge to any Hong Kong consumption tax. Accordingly, there is no export VAT refund claim to substantiate. For profits tax, export income may be taxable if the source of the income is in Hong Kong, but the relevant determination is made under the territorial source principle in sections 14 and 15 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, not through a VAT rate. While Hong Kong law imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, the 180-day benchmark in this dossier reflects the PRC State Administration of Foreign Exchange export-proceeds repatriation rule applicable where proceeds are settled through a mainland Chinese bank.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Hong Kong Import/Export Declaration (Trade Declaration) filed electronically with the Customs and Excise Department under the Import and Export (Registration) Regulations (Cap. 60E)
Commercial Invoice issued by the Hong Kong exporter or licensor
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing the physical movement of goods
Bank Credit Advice or Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency (where required by the receiving bank or foreign exchange regulator)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no VAT clawback mechanism in Hong Kong because no VAT/GST is imposed. However, false or inaccurate import/export declarations are subject to penalties under the Import and Export Ordinance (Cap. 60) and the Import and Export (Registration) Regulations (Cap. 60E), including fines up to HKD 50,000 and imprisonment up to six months. In addition, incorrect returns or false statements in any tax filing may result in additional tax assessments and penalties under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), including additional tax up to three times the amount of undercharged tax under section 82A.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese foreign exchange regime operates under a strict capital account control framework administered by SAFE while current account transactions are generally freely convertible for genuine economic activities. For the CN_HK cross-border FIP, the partnership's domestic fast-casual franchise revenue is RMB-denominated current account income and can be freely used for local operating expenses, supply chain purchases, payroll and tax payments. However, the partnership is subject to a genuine transaction standard requiring complete underlying documentation for all cross-border payments and receipts. Outbound royalty payments to the Hong Kong licensor are classified as current account services and are permissible once the FIP has completed its SAFE foreign exchange registration, provided the payment reflects an arm's-length license agreement, a withholding tax certificate, and a customs/SAFE trade in services declaration. Profit distributions and capital liquidation proceeds are capital account items requiring audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates and either prior SAFE approval or a post-event filing depending on whether the partnership allocates profits to a resident or non-resident partner. The FIP must not net receivables and payables offshore, and all foreign currency flows must be routed through a designated domestic account at a licensed bank. The use of offshore digital EMIs as the primary settlement rail would violate the statutory requirement that cross-border flows be transacted through licensed domestic financial institutions and reported to SAFE.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE Circular 2012 No. 1 and related update notices, all export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to a domestic foreign exchange settlement account within 90 days from the date of customs declaration for goods exports, or within 90 days from the due date of an export service contract for service exports such as franchising and master licensing fees. There is no mandatory conversion ratio currently in force; the FIP may retain the foreign exchange in its settlement account during the statutory retention period, but must verify all receipts within the SAFE online system on a monthly cycle. All retained foreign exchange must be used for legitimate current account transactions, and any conversion to RMB must be executed at a licensed bank at the prevailing counter rate. For the FIP's royalty income received from overseas sub-franchisees, the funds must be credited to a designated current account and settled or retained only after submission of the intellectual property license agreement, tax invoices and supporting revenue reconciliation to the bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FEA) and Capital Settlement Account (RMB)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational RMB Currency Account with integrated SAFE trade reporting
Cross-border Royalty Disbursement and Trade Settlement Account
Domestic RMB Operational Account with POS clearing and merchant aggregation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for the primary treasury blueprint. Offshore digital EMIs operating under Hong Kong or Singapore e-money licenses are not licensed banks in mainland China and cannot join China's domestic payment and clearing infrastructure (CNAPS), nor can they register with SAFE as cross-border settlement institutions. PBOC regulations require all RMB and foreign currency cross-border receipts and payments for a mainland-incorporated entity to be processed through a licensed domestic financial institution that performs direct SAFE reporting. An offshore EMI could act only as an auxiliary collection point for non-mainland franchise fees in HKD or USD, but receiving funds offshore without repatriation to the domestic designated account would breach the statutory surrender timeline and create an AML control gap. Therefore, the blueprint mandates exclusive use of Tier-1 commercial banks for all regulatory-critical flows, with EMIs rejected for any onshore RMB clearing or capital account movement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory representative and at least one authorised signatory of the Chinese FIP must physically attend the branch for the corporate account opening interview if the signatory is a natural person resident in mainland China. For the foreign Hong Kong corporate partner, physical appearance is generally waived if the ultimate beneficial owner appears in person at the same Chinese bank's Hong Kong branch and completes the inter-branch client due diligence; alternatively, a notarised and legalised Power of Attorney issued in Hong Kong and authenticated under mainland civil procedure may authorise a resident manager to complete the full in-branch interview. Remote consular proxy opening alone is not permitted for a Foreign-Invested Partnership because the bank is required by SAFE to verify the identities of the general partner and at least one site controller in person on the Chinese mainland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity: the FIP is a pass-through partnership whose HK corporate partner may be a non-operated holding vehicle, and AML screening flags a concentration of ownership through multiple low-substance layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full signed partnership agreement with a chain-of-ownership diagram showing each natural person and corporate entity from the FIP up to the ultimate controllers; Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate and Companies Registry annual return; UBO declaration naming every natural person holding 10% or more of the partnership; certificate of good standing for the HK partner; notarised and apostilled copies of passports and board resolutions; bank statements of the HK partner proving the source of capital; and a certified capital subscription breakdown with provenance of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty flow mismatch and transfer pricing red flags: outbound royalty rates for a broth bowl franchise master licensing model may exceed industry benchmarks, creating a concern about earnings stripping and structured AML evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An execution-ready arm's-length royalty agreement prepared under OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; a licensed Chinese IP valuation report substantiating the royalty rate; a comparability analysis referencing national and regional franchise royalty benchmarks of 3% to 8% of net sales; the Hong Kong profit tax return and Chinese withholding tax filing certificate; the SAFE trade in services declaration; and a monthly royalty calculation workbook generated from the POS system covering store-level revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash and QR heavy local receipts: fast-casual self-serve operations generate high volumes of low-value cash, QR code and mobile payment transactions, which align with potential smurfing or underreported revenue typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Integrated POS daily reconciliation reports; bank statements for all merchant settlement accounts; an audit trail linking POS transactions to the revenue journal; signed contracts with licensed UnionPay and Alipay acquirers; cash handling and daily cash deposit policy log; and PRC tax returns with VAT settlement certificates showing platform-reported revenue in the same amounts as the FIP's books.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and cross-border structured ambiguity: the HK licensor or the FIP may have indirect counterparty exposure to sanctioned territories or may appear to rely on a Hong Kong shell lacking economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Name-screening report from Dow Jones, Thomson Reuters or equivalent covering the FIP, all partners and all franchisors; business activity evidence including licensed restaurant testimonials, master franchise agreements and PRC/HK trademark registrations; a list of ultimate operational territories with sanctions screening; an economic substance evidence pack for the HK entity showing office lease, local employees and board minutes; and a sworn affidavit by the general partner undertaking immediate disclosure of any sanction-related ownership or change in control.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from the Hong Kong partner must be initiated as a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from a licensed Hong Kong corporate bank to the FIP's Foreign Exchange Capital Account at Bank of China or ICBC. The beneficiary account name must exactly match the FIP's SAFE foreign exchange registration, and the remittance reference must clearly state 'Capital contribution under FIP partnership agreement dated [date] - SAFE FDI Registration No. [XXXX]'. The receiving bank will classify the flow under the SAFE capital transaction code for direct investment equity capital contributions and conduct electronic foreign exchange registration. Within 30 days of receipt, the FIP must engage a certified public accountant in mainland China to issue a capital verification report, filing a copy with the local Administration for Market Regulation. The foreign currency may then be converted into RMB into a dedicated settlement account for payment, but the converted funds cannot be used for securities or lending outside the business scope described in the FIP registration. All transfers from the settlement account to local operating accounts will be subject to the bank's 24-hour post-transaction compliance review and SAFE system confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound royalty and licensing disbursements to the Hong Kong master franchisor will be executed using SWIFT MT103 transfers from the FIP's RMB operating account after conversion to HKD or USD through the bank's counter rate. The bank must hold on file the royalty agreement, the withholding tax certificate, the original invoice, and the POS-sourced royalty computation schedule to satisfy SAFE ex post verification. For physical franchise equipment imported from Hong Kong or third countries, the FIP should use a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued through ICBC or Bank of China for a sight tenor, with settlement against transport documents, commercial invoices and insurance certificates; alternative Documentary Collections under URC522 are permissible for established low-value suppliers. Local POS receipts from franchise stores will be settled daily through UnionPay and major QR aggregators directly into the FIP's domestic RMB operational account; surplus proceeds may be converted for royalty remittances only after the supporting trade documentation is approved by the bank's compliance desk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: SAFE-registered deliverable FX forward contract on USD/HKD vs RMB up to 12 months, supported by the underlying royalty or franchise agreement and limited to real current account exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swap (fixed-to-floating) for medium-term partnership capital exposures, subject to SAFE real-demand verification on the actual loan or capital structure

Zero-cost collar or window forward structure to convert HKD royalty income into RMB while preserving downward conversion rate flexibility, provided all legs are onshore deliverable and referenced to the onshore RMB rate

Non-deliverable forwards and offshore CNH-linked instruments are prohibited for the onshore FIP; the partnership may only trade deliverable FX contracts with licensed domestic banks under a genuine underlying foreign currency exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office (BRO) under the Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the expiry date of the current Business Registration Certificate (anniversary of initial registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a penalty of HKD 300 (approx USD 38) per month; failure to renew for 3 months may lead to cancellation of the business registration and administrative strike-off, with potential prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the issue date of the return (typically issued on 1 April for fiscal year ending 31 December, due 1 May; extension to 15 August may be granted for partnerships with accounting year ending 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of HKD 1,200 (approx USD 154) for the first offence, escalating to HKD 10,000 and 3 months imprisonment for persistent failure; the IRD may issue an estimated assessment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Gross income exceeding HKD 500,000 (approx USD 64,000) requires submission of audited financial statements with the Profits Tax Return. Additionally, if the partnership is structured as a Limited Partnership Fund (LPF), an annual audit by a certified public accountant is mandatory regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) aligned with IFRS; for small entities, the HKFRS for Private Entities (SME Standard) may be applied.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No statutory UBO register is required for partnerships. However, any change in partnership composition (admission, retirement, or transfer of profit share) must be reported to the Business Registration Office within 30 days. Annual confirmation of UBO details is not mandated, but the partnership must maintain accurate records of partners for tax purposes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Business Registration Certificate displayed at principal place of business

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (unincorporated business rate; two-tiered: 7.5% on first HK$2 million, 15% above)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays; available deductions include 100% deduction for R&D expenses (with 300% super deduction for qualifying R&D), capital allowances, and territorial source principle exempting offshore profits. Losses can be carried forward indefinitely.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form BIR52 (Profits Tax Return – Partnerships) filed via eTAX electronic filing system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 1 month of the issue date of the return; extensions may be granted upon application, typically up to 3 months for partnerships with accounting periods ending on 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the partnership's registered name and principal place of business in Hong Kong. For non-resident partners, ensure the address is a valid Hong Kong address for service of notices.
Enter the BR number from the Business Registration Office. This is mandatory for all partnerships, including those with non-resident partners.

Enter the period covered by the return, typically the fiscal year ending on 31 March or 31 December. For non-resident partners, ensure the basis period aligns with the partnership's accounting period and the partner's tax year in their home jurisdiction.

Enter the net assessable profits or adjusted losses for the basis period. For non-resident partners, allocate profits according to the partnership agreement and ensure proper allocation of income from Hong Kong sources. Apply the territorial source principle to exclude offshore profits.

After deducting allowable expenses and capital allowances, enter the assessable profits. For non-resident partners, apply the territorial source principle to determine Hong Kong-sourced profits. Ensure that any income from franchise licensing is correctly sourced to Hong Kong if the licensing activity occurs in Hong Kong.

Compute the tax at the partnership rate (15% for unincorporated businesses) on the assessable profits. For non-resident partners, the tax is assessed on the partnership as a whole, and each partner is liable for their share. The partnership must file the return and pay the tax, but partners may be jointly and severally liable.

List each partner's name, address, and share of profits. For non-resident partners, provide their tax identification numbers and tax residency certificates. This is critical for claiming treaty benefits and for the Inland Revenue Department to assess each partner's liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: HK$1,200 for late filing, plus an additional HK$10,000 if the return is filed more than 6 months late. For willful evasion, penalties up to 200% of tax undercharged and imprisonment up to 3 years. Failure to file may also result in estimated assessments and additional penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Hong Kong does not impose withholding tax on dividends)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since no WHT is imposed on dividends, no DTA relief is required. For royalties and interest, if any, the DTA with China provides for reduced rates. To claim treaty benefits, the non-resident must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Chinese tax authorities, complete a beneficial ownership declaration (Form IR1313), and substantiate that the recipient is the beneficial owner of the income. The application must be made before the payment or within the prescribed time frame to avoid full statutory withholding.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 4.95% (for corporations) or 4.5% (for unincorporated) on gross royalties derived from Hong Kong; under DTA with China, reduced to 5% (but since statutory is lower, the DTA rate may not apply). Interest: no withholding tax on interest paid to non-residents unless the interest is derived from a Hong Kong business; under DTA, interest is exempt from Hong Kong tax.
